sourcedFrom: Ruger 22 Charger Standard, Takedown, & Takedown Lite Instruction Manual — PM200 (2023)
cleanIntro: The 22 Charger comes out of its stock for cleaning, and there is one detail that will damage the stock if you get it wrong — read step 3.

steps.title: Clear it, hammer cocked
steps.action: Point the pistol in a safe direction, engage the safety if the hammer is cocked, remove the magazine, fully retract the bolt and look into the chamber. Let the bolt close; the hammer should be cocked.
steps.prose: The hammer state matters here — the manual expects it cocked going into the strip.
steps.quote: fully retract the bolt and visually make certain there is not a cartridge in the chamber. Then allow the bolt to close. The hammer should be cocked.
steps.cite: Ruger 22 Charger Standard, Takedown, & Takedown Lite Instruction Manual — PM200 — Disassembly, step 1, p.20
steps.warn: Always unload a firearm before cleaning, lubrication, disassembly, or assembly.

steps.title: Loosen — do not remove — the takedown screw
steps.action: On a standard 22 Charger, loosen the takedown screw without removing it. On a Takedown model, first follow the manual’s "Removing the Barrel Assembly" procedure, then loosen the takedown screw on the receiver assembly.
steps.prose: Two different starting points depending on which Charger you own; the manual covers both.
steps.quote: loosen (do not remove) the takedown screw
steps.cite: Ruger 22 Charger Standard, Takedown, & Takedown Lite Instruction Manual — PM200 — Disassembly, step 2, p.20

steps.title: Centre the safety or you will damage the stock
steps.action: Position the safety so an equal amount of the button shows on each side before lifting the receiver assembly out.
steps.prose: This is not a preference. Ruger states the stock will be damaged if the safety is off-centre when the receiver comes out.
steps.caution: If the safety is not in the middle when the receiver assembly is lifted out of the stock, the stock will be damaged.
steps.quote: If the safety is not in the middle when the receiver assembly is lifted out of the stock, the stock will be damaged.
steps.cite: Ruger 22 Charger Standard, Takedown, & Takedown Lite Instruction Manual — PM200 — Disassembly, step 3, p.20
steps.warn: If the safety is not in the middle when the receiver assembly is lifted out of the stock, the stock will be damaged.

steps.title: Swing the receiver up and out
steps.action: Swing the receiver assembly upward away from the forearm of the stock, watching that the two receiver cross pins and the bolt stop pin do not fall out.
steps.prose: Three small pins, and they will roll off a bench.
steps.quote: Be careful the two receiver cross pins and bolt stop pin do not fall out.
steps.cite: Ruger 22 Charger Standard, Takedown, & Takedown Lite Instruction Manual — PM200 — Disassembly, step 4, p.20

deepSteps.title: Trigger guard out — as a unit
deepSteps.action: Drift out the two receiver cross pins and lift the trigger guard away.
deepSteps.prose: Keep it as one assembly. Ruger recommends not disassembling the components from the trigger guard.
deepSteps.caution: It is recommended that the components of the trigger guard assembly not be disassembled from the trigger guard.
deepSteps.quote: Remove the trigger guard by simply drifting out the two receiver cross pins.
deepSteps.cite: Ruger 22 Charger Standard, Takedown, & Takedown Lite Instruction Manual — PM200 — Disassembly, step 5, p.20

cleaning.name: BORE & CHAMBER
tasks: Solvent patch, correctly sized brush, then dry patches until clean
Rimfire fouling is waxy — the chamber needs the same attention as the bore

cleaning.name: BOLT & RECEIVER
tasks: Wipe the bolt face and around the extractor
Clean the receiver interior and bolt raceways
Light oil on bearing surfaces only

reassembly: Seat the receiver assembly back into the stock with the safety still centred.
fncheck: With the magazine out and chamber confirmed empty, check the safety blocks the trigger and the bolt cycles freely.
